## Interaction from lecture 18

```{r l18-interaction-plot, echo=FALSE, fig.width=7, fig.height=4.3}
source("../../_setup.R")
rmData <- read.csv(datasetsPath("RM_ANOVA_AlcoholSpeedTime.csv"))
# Rows alcohol, columns speed (columns are none_alc_none_speed, none_alc_some_speed, ...).
cellMeans <- matrix(colMeans(rmData[, grep("_alc_", names(rmData))]), nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE)
par(cex = 1.0, cex.lab = 1.1)
plot(1:3, cellMeans[, 1], type = "n", ylim = c(0, 10), xlim = c(0.8, 3.2), xaxt = "n", bty = "n", las = 1,
     xlab = "Alcohol", ylab = "Mean accidents")
axis(1, at = 1:3, labels = c("none", "some", "much"))
for (j in 1:3) {
  lines(1:3, cellMeans[, j], lwd = 2)
  points(1:3, cellMeans[, j], pch = c(21, 22, 23)[j], bg = "white", cex = 2, lwd = 2)
}
legend("bottomright", legend = c("none", "some", "much"), pch = c(21, 22, 23), pt.bg = "white", lwd = 2,
       title = "Speed", bty = "n", cex = 1.0)
```

# Closing

## Recap

- Non-parametric tests are rank-based, which means they are robust to:
  - Non-normality
  - Transformations of the data
  - Outliers
